dedupe_keys.name: 5g lena 5g nr module for the ns 3 simulator

description: 5G-LENA is an open-source, 3GPP-compliant 5G New Radio simulator built as a pluggable module for the ns-3 discrete-event network simulator. It models the full stack from the application layer down to the physical layer for end-to-end performance evaluation, algorithm design and reproducible research. The project site lists a roadmap from the first NR release in 2019 through 3GPP 38.901 channels and dual-polarised MIMO (2022), QoS and XR traffic (2023), full SU-MIMO and fronthaul (2024) to CSI-RS, multi-panel and AI features (2025) and QoS flows, handover, RRC, spatial consistency and Sionna ray tracing (2026); the current release is NR-v5.1. The module is designed, developed and maintained by the OpenSim unit of CTTC in Castelldefels, Spain, and inherits ns-3's multi-RAT support, so NR, NR-U, LTE, Wi-Fi and WiGig can coexist in one scenario. Coverage is generic: any deployment the user configures. Access: source and documentation through the project site, which links to the software download and a user group. Licence and cost: GPLv2, free of charge. Caveats: the site says it is calibrated against 3GPP campaigns but the page read gives no validation figures, and 6G items (NTN, ISAC, RIS) are listed as future work. It suits capacity and performance studies of radio access networks, spectrum coexistence experiments and as the radio layer of a telecom digital twin. It complements the ns-3 platform (platform-ns-3) and the NIST O-RAN module (model-nist-ns3-oran).
